title: Year 8 Summer 1 end of half-term quiz: angles and area
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y8 lesson 69 (Year 8 Summer 1 end of half-term quiz: angles and area (portal quiz, secure mode, written for this unit))
intro: Covers lessons 11 to 69 of Angles, area and symmetry. Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: A triangle has base 10 cm, other sides 8 cm and 7 cm, and perpendicular height 5 cm. Its area is:
questions.a: B) 25 cm². ½ × 10 × 5 = 25. 40 uses the 8 cm side; 50 forgets to halve; 35 uses the 7 cm side.

questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 5 m and 9 m and height 6 m. Its area is:
questions.a: A) 42 m². ½ × 14 × 6 = 42. 84 forgets to halve; 270 multiplies all three numbers.

questions.q: In a Z shape between parallel lines, one angle is 48°. The other is:
questions.a: A) 48°. Alternate angles are equal: 48°. 132° is the angle on a straight line with 48°.

questions.q: Co-interior angles are 2x° and (x + 30)°. x =
questions.a: A) 50. 2x + x + 30 = 180, so 3x = 150 and x = 50 (angles 100° and 80°). 30 sets the angles equal, which is the rule for alternate angles.

questions.q: Which is a proof, not a demonstration?
options: an argument with alternate angles that works for any triangle
questions.a: B) an argument with alternate angles that works for any triangle. Only the argument from facts that are always true covers every triangle. Measuring, however many, only shows the ones measured.

questions.q: The angle sum of a hexagon is:
questions.a: A) 720°. (6 - 2) × 180 = 720. 1080 comes from 6 × 180, which counts too many triangles.

questions.q: A regular polygon has exterior angles of 40°. The number of sides is:
Which regular polygon tessellates on its own?
questions.a: A) hexagon. 120° × 3 = 360°. Pentagons (108°), octagons (135°) and decagons (144°) do not divide 360° exactly.

questions.q: A 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle has a triangle of base 10 cm and height 4 cm on top. The total area is:
questions.a: A) 80 cm². 60 + ½ × 10 × 4 = 60 + 20 = 80. 100 forgets to halve the triangle.

questions.q: 0.5 m² in cm² is:
questions.a: C) 5000. 0.5 × 10 000 = 5000. 50 uses × 100, the length factor.

questions.q: A circle has radius 3 cm. Its circumference is about:
questions.a: B) 18.8 cm. 2 × π × 3 = 18.85. 9.4 treats the radius as the diameter; 28.3 is the area.

questions.q: A circle has diameter 8 cm. Its area is:
questions.a: A) 16π cm². r = 4, so π × 4² = 16π. 64π uses the diameter; 8π is the circumference.

questions.q: The perimeter of a semicircle of diameter 4 cm is:
questions.a: A) 2π + 4 cm. Half of π × 4 is 2π, plus the 4 cm diameter. 2π forgets the straight edge.

questions.q: The order of rotational symmetry of a regular pentagon is:
questions.a: A) 5. It fits onto itself every 72°, five times in a full turn. 10 counts lines and turns together.

questions.q: Reflect (2, 5) in the x-axis:
questions.a: A) (2, -5). The x-axis is horizontal: x stays, y changes sign. (-2, 5) is the reflection in the y-axis.

questions.q: Reflect (3, -1) in the line y = x:
questions.a: A) (-1, 3). Swap the coordinates: (-1, 3). (1, -3) also changes the signs, which is the rule for y = -x.

questions.q: The area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm is:
questions.a: B) 30 cm²

questions.q: A parallelogram has base 7 cm and height 4 cm. Its area is:
questions.a: A) 28 cm²

questions.q: Alternate angles are:
questions.a: A) equal
